metadata.name: Postmodernism
metadata.description: A philosophical current questioning totalising accounts of progress, universal authority and fixed identity, assessed through its pluralist and anti-disciplinary political implications.
metadata.period: Political reading of Lyotard and related French critical thought, 1970s–1980s
metadata.scope: A provisional political interpretation centered on Lyotard’s rejection of totalising narratives and Foucault’s critique of disciplinary power. Postmodernism is not a unified electoral or economic platform; no claim of unanimity across its authors is made. This is a provisional, scoped interpretation, not a survey of adherents. Modern applications and five-point intensities are inferred. The cited sources establish context; they do not document answers to every quiz statement.
metadata.phrase: Society should leave room for diverse forms of life and knowledge, question claims to universal authority and resist institutions that silence difference.
